paper_title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for   Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
caption: Number of questions, out of 40, where CoT generated by GPT3 using different methods has at least 1 factual error. Factual errors: < OneR < NoR.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of questions with at least one factual error in the CoT generated by GPT3 using different methods. The horizontal axis lists four datasets: HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC; the axis is labeled with dataset names in no particular order. The vertical axis represents the number of questions with factual errors, labeled as "Factual Errors" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 40, marked with intervals of 5. The chart displays three types of bars, each representing a different method: NoR QA (orange with white dots), OneR QA (red with white dots), and IRCot QA (blue with diagonal stripes), as indicated by the legend. For each dataset, the NoR QA bar is the tallest, with values of approximately 15 for HotpotQA, 29 for 2WikiMQA, 28 for MuSiQue, and 15 for IIRC. The OneR QA bars have values of around 10 for HotpotQA, 23 for 2WikiMQA, 27 for MuSiQue, and 14 for IIRC. The IRCot QA bars have values of about 5 for HotpotQA, 14 for 2WikiMQA, 23 for MuSiQue, and 11 for IIRC. The bars are not sorted in any specific order, and there is no visual emphasis on any of the bars. Overall, the chart presents a clear comparison of the number of questions with factual errors across different datasets and methods.
